purpose: Guanfacine is used to treat attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adults, helping improve focus, attention, and impulse control. The extended-release form (Intuniv) is specifically approved for ADHD. The immediate-release form (Tenex) is also sometimes used to treat high blood pressure.
how_it_works: Guanfacine works by calming certain overactive signals in the brain, particularly in an area called the prefrontal cortex, which helps with self-control and focus. It acts like a gentle brake on the 'stress response' part of the brain, helping your thoughts become more organized and reducing impulsive behavior. Unlike stimulant ADHD medications, it does not speed up the brain — it helps quiet the noise so you can concentrate better.
common_side_effects: Sleepiness or drowsiness (especially when starting), low blood pressure, dizziness, headache, dry mouth, stomach upset or nausea, constipation, and irritability. Many of these improve after the first few weeks as your body adjusts.
warnings: Do not stop taking guanfacine suddenly — this can cause your blood pressure to spike quickly, which can be dangerous. Always taper off slowly under your doctor's guidance. It can lower your blood pressure and heart rate, so be careful when standing up quickly to avoid dizziness or fainting. Avoid alcohol as it can increase drowsiness. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some can interact with guanfacine.
typical_dosing: For ADHD (extended-release, Intuniv): usually started at 1 mg once daily, taken at the same time each day, and gradually increased up to 4–7 mg per day depending on age and response. For blood pressure (Tenex): typically 1 mg at bedtime, adjusted as needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never adjust the dose on your own.
